## What We Did 

Reviewed R basics including dplyr and tidycensus. 

## Key Concepts 

Data Visualization: 
- Anscombe's Quartet --> why visualization is important

Plot is a mapping from columns in your data to visual properties on your page. 
("grammar of graphics" = "gg")


Your Data:                   Page (Canvas):

estimate -------------------> position on the y-axis
population -----------------> position on the x-axis 
viability ------------------> color
MOE ------------------------> size 


**How ggplot works**

1. p <- ggplot(data) -- creates a blank canvas
2. aes(...) -- aesthetic mappings - NO DECORATING! Just business.
3. geom_*() -- the shape/type of chart 


ex. 

ggplot(tract_data) + 
  aes(x = population, y = moe_pct) +
  geom_point() 
  
  
What I want to know| GEOM
-------------------|------------------
                   |
how a variable is  | geom_histogram()
spread             |
--------------------------------------

variables relate?  | geom_point()
--------------------------------------

**Coefficient of Variation (CV)** 

- relative measure of sampling error 

standard error 
--------------    x 100   
  estimate
  

Census Bureau = 15% is high reliability 
                30% is high sampling error 
                

**Derived Uncertainty**

poverty rate = # in poverty <--- has an moe
              -------------
                  total     <--- has an moe
                  
tidycensus has built in functions to address this
- moe_sum() --> adding estimates together 
- moe_prop() --> one estimate as a share of another 
- moe_ratio() --> pov #      one not a subset of the other 
                  ----
                  HH income 
                  
Change over TIME

1) issue: the overlapping intervals 
   2019 - 2023, 2018-2023 --- these datasets share four years of the same data
 
   solution: compare with non-overlapping intervals --- 2014-2018 vs 2019-2023
   
2) issue: margins of error 
   ex.  2014-2018 -- $45,000 w a moe of 8,000
        2019-2023 -- $62,000 w a moe of 11,000
        
   solution: calculate standard error of difference 
             SE difference = sqrt(SE1^2/1.645 + SE2^2/1.645)  
      
             z = (est1 - est2) / SE diff
             
Confidence Interval of Change 

Difference +/- (1.645 * SEdiff)
Interval  = 3,339 - 30,601  ---- this is our range, taking in low end and high end of estimate,                                    we can be 90% sure that incomes went up
